concept.name: Red cards and playing with 10 men

scenes.narration: Crystal Palace just lost two-nil at Tottenham, and the game turned early, when one of their players was shown a red card. So what does a red card actually do?

visual.text: Spurs revival continues with victory over 10-man Crystal Palace

scenes.narration: In football, the referee can show two cards. A yellow card is a warning. A red card means the player is sent off, straight away, for the rest of the match.
There are two ways to get a red card. A really serious foul, like a dangerous tackle, is a straight red. Or two yellow cards in the same game add up to a red.
And here's the key part. Nobody can come on to replace that player, so the team plays the rest of the game with ten people instead of eleven.
Imagine a group project where one teammate walks out, but the workload stays the same. Everyone else has to run more, cover more space and get tired faster.
That's what happened to Palace. Jean-Philippe Mateta was shown an early red card, so his team had to play a player short for a long time.

visual.text: Jean-Philippe Mateta was shown an early red card

scenes.narration: Tottenham won two-nil, their third Premier League win in a row for the first time in twenty months. For Palace, it was a third straight league defeat, and more pressure on manager Pierre Sage.

lines: 3 wins in a row for Spurs
3 defeats in a row for Palace

scenes.narration: Next time you watch a match, keep an eye on the cards. One red card can change tactics, wear a team out and decide the result.
Quick recap: a red card sends a player off with no replacement. Ready to test yourself?

quiz.question: A player who already has a yellow card commits another foul and gets a second yellow. What happens?
options: It becomes a red card and he is sent off
Nothing, because yellow cards reset at half-time
He must be swapped for a substitute
The other team gets an automatic penalty
quiz.explanation: Two yellow cards in one match add up to a red card, and a sent-off player can't be replaced.

lesson.takeaway: A red card sends a player off with no replacement, so their team plays the rest of the match a player short.
